clue.text: Representative in "the Cheshire cheese"?

indicators.note: the word in signals that the representative sits inside the Cheshire creature

parts.note: the Cheshire Cat is the grinning feline in Alice in Wonderland, so 'the Cheshire' stands for that animal
a representative in parliament is a member

explanation.surface: A question about who represents an old London pub called the Cheshire Cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks suggest the famous Fleet Street pub, Ye Olde Cheshire Cheese, but 'the Cheshire' is Lewis Carroll's grinning cat and 'cheese' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft creamy French variety from Normandy, so an example of the dairy product named.

clue.text: Greed for a very adult staple food

parts.note: A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult
rice is a staple food across much of the world

explanation.surface: Greed is portrayed as wanting a really grown-up basic diet.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an insatiable desire for wealth or possessions.

clue.text: Made possible by being fit in final

indicators.note: the word in tells us the fit word goes inside the final word

parts.note: the final part of something is its end
fit, as in capable, means able

explanation.surface: Someone reached the final because they were fit enough to compete.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to allow or empower something to happen.

clue.text: The legal profession misses these workers

parts.note: barristers collectively are called the Bar
misses, young unmarried women, are maids

explanation.surface: Lawyers lament the absence of certain employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misses' reads as a verb (feels the lack of) but is a plural noun: young women, or maids.
explanation.definitionFit: Women serving drinks in a pub are workers of this kind, the ones the clue itself builds.

clue.text: A strong desire to deliver shirt on time

indicators.note: to deliver here is read as to free or release the letters of shirt into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is keen to get a shirt delivered punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to deliver' is an unusual anagram signal: read it as setting the letters free to land in a fresh order.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a craving or longing, as in a thirst for knowledge.

clue.text: Party promises to reveal nothing

parts.note: to manifest something is to reveal or display it
O, the zero shape, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A cynic says a political party's promises reveal nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A political party publishes its election pledges in this kind of document.

clue.text: Attack bees swarming around one, for example

indicators.note: around tells us the jumbled bees enclose the other pieces
bees swarming move about in disorder, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A swarm of bees attacks someone, perhaps as an illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bees swarming' looks like the attackers in the story, but 'swarming' scrambles the bees into BESE, which then goes 'around' the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to surround and assail a place, as an army does a town.

clue.text: Paparazzi's risky ventures

parts.note: photographers working at a distance with telephoto lenses take such pictures, and the phrase also means gambles with little chance of success

explanation.surface: Celebrity photographers take chances.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means an unlikely bet, while for a photographer it also means pictures taken from far off.

clue.text: Sailor's call for effort — gets the sack

definitions.meaning: the traditional chant sailors used when hauling ropes together
being given the sack means being dismissed from work

explanation.definitionFit: It is a rhythmic hauling cry at sea, and getting it means being thrown out or fired.

clue.text: Hack around Hackney — how ghastly!

indicators.note: around shows the horse word encloses the carriage word

parts.note: a hack is a horse for riding, and a mare is a female horse
a hackney carriage is the formal name for a taxi or cab

explanation.surface: A journalist goes round the London borough of Hackney and is horrified.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney looks like the London borough but is short for hackney carriage, a cab; 'Hack' is a riding horse, not a journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: gruesome or grim, concerned with death and horror.

clue.text: Call about trouble for fence

indicators.note: about tells us the phone call word goes round the trouble word

parts.note: to ring is to call on the telephone
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Someone phones to complain about a problem with a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier made of bars or posts, a kind of fencing.

clue.text: Poor individual taken in by poets' game

indicators.note: taken in by shows the poor individual is enclosed within the poets

parts.note: bards are poets
poor in the sense of unwell means ill
I, the Roman one, stands for an individual

explanation.surface: A poor person is fooled by poets playing a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue sport played on a cloth-covered table, so an example of a game.

clue.text: A long time after mother gets compensation

indicators.note: after places the long time following the mother word, which sits above it in the grid

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
ages means a long time

explanation.surface: Mum finally gets paid after waiting forever.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal term: money awarded by a court to make up for loss or injury.

clue.text: Where a swimmer turns in a protracted way

definitions.meaning: a swimmer in a pool turns at the end of each length
done at great extent or for a long while

explanation.definitionFit: Literally, at the end of a pool length; idiomatically, at great length or eventually.

clue.text: Finished behind Britain, bowed

indicators.note: behind places the finished word after the abbreviation for Britain

parts.note: finished means ended

explanation.surface: An athlete finished just behind the British competitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: bent, as in the archaic phrase on bended knee.

clue.text: Union member might have one veto

definitions.text: Union member might have one veto

parts.words: Union member might have one veto
parts.note: a trade union delegate may cast a single vote on behalf of all the members represented

explanation.surface: A trade unionist holds the power to block a motion.
explanation.definitionFit: A vote cast by one delegate counting for all the members they represent.

clue.text: Perceptive raptor (spotted)

parts.note: an eagle is a bird of prey, or raptor
spotted, as in seen, means eyed

explanation.surface: A bird of prey is noticed by an observant watcher.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: sharp-sighted and quick to notice detail.

clue.text: Mount an attack on USA, last to fall

indicators.note: to fall suggests the letters of USA and last tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: An enemy launches an attack on America, finally bringing it down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to fall' signals the anagram of USA and LAST together.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to attack physically or launch an offensive.

clue.text: Listen to storyteller on prison term for Australian flyer

indicators.note: listen to signals that the storyteller word is heard, not seen

parts.note: a storyteller in the sense of one who tells fibs is a liar
bird is British slang for a prison sentence, from rhyming slang bird-lime for time

explanation.surface: Hear a novelist talk about doing time, from someone flying in from Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listen to' tells you LIAR is heard as LYRE. 'Doing bird' is British slang for serving time in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A ground-dwelling songbird of Australia famed for its mimicry, so an example of a bird.

clue.text: Maiden to supply weapons and their method of delivery

parts.note: in cricket a maiden is an over in which no runs are scored
to arm is to supply weapons

explanation.surface: A young woman equips the army and describes how it was done.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored; overarm describes a bowler's delivery with the arm above the shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket bowlers deliver the ball with the arm raised above the shoulder in this style.

clue.text: Sings badly — notedly so, but not dismissed

indicators.note: badly signals the remaining letters are jumbled into a new order
dismissed tells us the word not is sent away from notedly

explanation.surface: Someone sings out of tune, remarkably so, yet keeps their place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissed' removes NOT from the start of NOTEDLY, leaving EDLY; with SO, 'badly' rearranges EDLYSO.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine singers perform in this warbling style that switches between chest voice and falsetto.

clue.text: Carters have to measure up people

indicators.note: up in a down clue reverses the measure word, reading it upwards

parts.note: a yard is a unit of measurement
men means people

explanation.surface: Delivery men have to size up the public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses YARD to DRAY in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Men who drove horse-drawn carts for deliveries, especially for breweries.

clue.text: Granting occupation to Latvian in government

parts.note: a Lett is a person from Latvia

explanation.surface: Permission to occupy is given to a Latvian joining a government.
explanation.definitionFit: Allowing a tenant to use property in return for rent.

clue.text: Polite untruths are said to educate

indicators.note: are said signals the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: untruths are lies, and polite means civil

explanation.surface: White lies told politely are said to be a form of education.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are said' tells you that CIVIL LIES is heard, giving the spelling CIVILISE.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to bring culture and refinement to a people.

clue.text: Red setter, for instance, finds tar

parts.note: the Red Sea, so red names a sea
a setter is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: An Irish red setter stumbles upon some tar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red setter' reads as the dog breed, but the words split: Red is a sea and setter a dog. 'tar' is old slang for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for a sailor, especially an experienced one.

clue.text: With sixth sense, managed to assimilate English language

indicators.note: assimilate means take in, so the English letter is absorbed into the run

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is the sixth sense
managed, as in ran a business, gives ran

explanation.surface: A psychic managed to learn English with intuition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With sixth sense' reads as a psychic's gift, but it is just the first piece; 'assimilate' takes the English letter into the following run, right after ESP.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificial international language invented by Zamenhof in 1887.

clue.text: Name of girl coming across Scottish mountain plant

indicators.note: coming across means spanning, so the girl's name goes round the mountain

parts.note: Vera is a girl's name
ben is the Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis

explanation.surface: A girl's name is encountered on a Scottish peak.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering garden species, also called vervain, so an example of the general term.

clue.text: Post accepted by high flyer

parts.note: letters taken on board an aircraft for delivery overseas

explanation.surface: An ambitious high achiever accepts a job offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail carried by aircraft, the high flyer that accepts it.

clue.text: Weapon used by party on hill exercises

indicators.note: on in an across clue places the party word after the hill and exercises pieces

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
PE is physical education, school exercises
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A weapon used at a party held during hill exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used by' is a link; 'on' means the party comes after the other two. A tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-propelled underwater missile, an example of a weapon.

clue.text: Times of happiness turn a legend fashionable

parts.note: a turn in a game is a go

indicators.note: fashionable in the sense of being fashioned, reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Turning a legend into something trendy brings happy times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' looks like the anagram signal, but it is the piece meaning a go; 'fashionable' is read as fashioned or reshaped, which scrambles A LEGEND into LDENAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a period of great prosperity or achievement.
